Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the demo last week. - A list of subprocessors involved in request handling, storage, and telemetry (including cloud regions).
- How routing/fallbacks work if a region is unavailable or if we pin to a region.
- Confirmation of deletion behavior for cached KV/prefixes and logs, and timelines.
- Which contractual controls you offer (DPA, SCCs, Data Processing Addenda, KMS/HSM options).

Can you provide a short one-page summary and a CSV with the current subprocessor roster? We need this for our vendor risk assessment (VRM) by EOD Monday.

Appreciate a concise, factual response we can pass to the security reviewers.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2025-05-04 15:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial Q - confirm locations, subprocessors, deletion TTLs

Jordan / Marissa — quick technical notes you can include verbatim: 

- Execution regions: Hosted API requests are served from our regional clusters. Primary processing regions currently: US (us-west-2, us-east-1), EU (eu-west-1, europe-west3), and APAC (asia-southeast1) for customers in those regions. Requests may transiently touch other regions only for routing/fallbacks or if a model variant is only available in a different region — we keep minimal transient hops and record them in audit logs.

- Subprocessors (high level): AWS (compute, S3) in listed regions; GCP (optional model cache) in europe-west3; Redis provider for KV caching (managed by Redwood in the customer's selected region when pinned); analytics/telemetry vendor (RedTemp Analytics) for aggregated telemetry (no PII). Dedicated and Private customers can require subprocessor restrictions via the DPA. For the CSV, we will include hostnames, region mapping, and SOC2 status.

- Routing & fallbacks: Default policy is latency-first within the chosen region group. If capacity is constrained we fail over to a compatible model variant in another region according to the routing policy in the DPA. Customers can request region pinning (no cross-region fallback) for Dedicated/Private deployments; hosted accounts can request strict region routing but with potential throughput tradeoffs.

- Deletion: Ephemeral KV/prefix cache TTLs default to 1 hour; model inference traces (non-payload) retained for 30 days for observability. Logs with request payloads are deleted on customer request; we support on-demand purge via the Console and have an erase API endpoint. Complete deletion (including backups) is committed within 90 days in our standard DPA; we can accelerate that in contractual terms for enterprise deals.

- Controls: We support DPA, standard SCCs, customer-managed KMS for encryption-at-rest, and HSM-backed key options for Private deployments. We can provide evidence (SOC2 report) and support vendor questionnaires.

Attaching subprocessors_inventory_20250504.csv (will fill with hostnames/regions/SOC2 link). Marissa — please add legal phrasing for SCCs/SRO and confirm the default cache TTLs and any regional restrictions we should call out.

-Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: subprocessors_inventory_20250504.csv]

Hi Lena — below is a concise Q&A and the subprocessors CSV is attached. You can paste this into your VRM intake. If you want any item tightened for contract, we can mark it as a contractual requirement (DPA addendum).

Q: Where are Redwood inference requests executed?
A: Hosted API requests are served from regional clusters. Primary regions: US (us-west-2, us-east-1), EU (eu-west-1, europe-west3), APAC (asia-southeast1). Transient cross-region hops are minimized and only occur for routing/fallbacks or when a specific model variant is provisioned in another region. All hops are logged in audit trails.

Q: Who are the subprocessors?
A: High-level: AWS (compute, S3) in listed regions, GCP (model cache in europe-west3), a managed Redis provider for KV caching (regionally deployed where possible), and an analytics vendor for aggregated telemetry (no PII). Full roster with hostnames, region mapping, and compliance links attached (subprocessors_inventory_20250504.csv). Dedicated/Private customers can request subprocessor restrictions in the DPA.

Q: What happens if our pinned region is unavailable?
A: For Hosted customers we have a routing policy that prefers the pinned region; if capacity is unavailable we will fail over to a compatible model in another region according to the policy unless a contractual region-lock is requested. For Dedicated/Private customers you can prohibit cross-region failover; in those cases requests will queue or fail based on the configured SLA. We'll include suggested contract language for either behavior.

Q: How is cached data and logs deleted?
A: Ephemeral KV/prefix caches default TTL = 1 hour. Inference traces (non-payload observability data) retained 30 days. Request payloads and logs are deletable on-demand via Console or the erase API and are purged from active storage immediately; full removal including backups is completed within 90 days under our standard DPA. Enterprise addenda can shorten the backup purge window and require customer-managed KMS/HSM.

Q: What contractual and technical controls do you offer?
A: DPA, SCCs, customer-managed KMS, optional HSM-backed keys for Private installs, SOC2 report availability, and per-route audit logs. We can include explicit subprocessor consent language and region-lock clauses in the DPA.

If you want us to mark any of these as mandatory in the contract we can produce redline-ready language. Please confirm whether StellarHealth requires EU-only execution with no cross-region fallback or whether the standard hosted policy is acceptable.

Best regards,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: subprocessors_inventory_20250504.csv, geo-processing-summary.pdf]
